title: Final review of the Phase 4 diff
description:
Review the epic diff outside-in. Weight it toward what a green suite cannot see — Phase 2 found twelve boundary defects by running, Phase 3 found five by reviewing against Phase 2's list, and this epic adds autonomy, which removes the human who would otherwise notice.

Named passes this epic earns:
- CREDENTIAL GRADE. Can a read-only run push by any route — including calling GitHub directly rather than through the factory? Is the grade enforced where it is claimed to be?
- BRANCH OWNERSHIP. Can CI remediation reach a branch a human owns, through any path including a mis-parsed branch name?
- LOOP TERMINATION. Flake gate and strike budget: find the input that makes either loop forever or spend without converging.
- UNATTENDED FAILURE. Everything here runs with nobody watching. For each loop, what does it do when it fails at 3am, and is that visible the next morning?

2026-08-24 19:37 - Findings adjudicated:
- Pass 3's HIGH (a struck-out branch silently resumes spending when the rolling window rolls over, and never pages again) plus the missing top-level catch and the epicOfBranch cleanup go to tick uls, which BLOCKS closeout. The ci_escalation table having two writes and zero reads is the kind of finding that only comes from reading the code rather than the tests.
- Pass 2's design gap (branch ownership is namespace-prefix trust, and tick/<id> is a namespace humans and herdr already use in this repo) is filed as am2, P1, not blocking. The branded type holds against parsing attacks, which is what meo claimed; the residual is a naming collision, and whether to require a positive record is the operator's call.
- Pass 4's scope question (sweeps and PR review have no proactive failure visibility) is filed as zaw. Same class as Phase 2's hardest lesson one level up: there a supervisor could not report its own death, here a loop can fail nightly and nothing says so.
- Passes 1 and 2's structural halves came back clean, and the reviewer went looking properly — it checked the sandbox environment, the git remote, credential helpers and the image for a second credential before accepting pzf's claim.

The review's own STATUS said Phase 4 should not close until Pass 3 is routed. Agreed, and it is.

closed_reason: Completed: final review of the Phase 4 diff. Credential grade clean — no bypass found, enforced at token-mint time and verified end to end. Branch ownership structurally sound against parsing attacks with one acknowledged design gap. One confirmed HIGH in loop termination: the strike budget bounds each 24-hour window but not the branch, so an escalated branch silently reopens. One confirmed bug: an unhandled throw on the CI webhook path bypasses the loop's own escalation. All routed to uls, am2 and zaw.
